error_reason: The orchestrator directed data collection around IMDb filmography (ratings and runtimes) without first constraining the candidate set to titles available on Netflix (US) and under 150 minutes. This mis-specified plan oriented the run toward broad film data rather than the intersection of constraints required by the task, leading downstream to select Glass Onion without validating Netflix US availability and runtime against the highest IMDb rating within the constrained set.

hypotheses.rationale: The orchestrator directed WebSurfer to scrape an IMDb page for Daniel Craig 'movies' with ratings and durations, implicitly restricting to IMDb’s Daniel Craig filmography rather than first defining the set of candidate titles that are both under 150 minutes and available on Netflix (US). This early mis-specification set the workflow to collect broad filmography data instead of aligning steps to the end criterion (Netflix US availability + <150 min + highest IMDb rating). It primed later steps to check availability title-by-title without consolidating or comparing ratings properly, culminating in the incorrect selection of 'Casino Royale' instead of 'Glass Onion.' Correcting this step to structure data collection around the final constraints (including current Netflix US availability and runtime filter) would have prevented the wrong conclusion.
hypotheses.check: Verify whether step 6’s instruction established a plan to collect and compare: (a) Netflix US availability, (b) IMDb ratings, and (c) runtimes <150, and to rank the intersection accordingly. Compare with later selection at step 88 where 'Casino Royale' is chosen despite 'Glass Onion' meeting criteria and being higher rated on IMDb.
